title: Deferred tool synthesis with feedback fences and recursion sentinel
creator: Aisha Rios
description: Introduce a deferred/one-shot tool synthesis stage in the execution loop that: (1) delays expensive tool result marshaling until downstream consumers are certain they need it (stream-aware), (2) applies a feedback fence for injected results so model-generated content cannot trigger unbounded tool recursion, and (3) provides a compatibility shim for older tool contracts that expect eager JSON blobs. This reduces unnecessary CPU/GPU cycles for large KV caches, lowers latency for short streaming responses, and hardens safety against recursive tool calls.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end bench shows >= 12% median token-cost reduction on mixed chat+tool workloads compared to current eager-injection baseline
No new end-to-end p95 latency regressions > 5% for 95% of routes in runtime-staging
Compatibility shim allows legacy tools (v1 tool contract) to work without code changes; demonstrate with internal search_tool_v1 integration
Recursion sentinel prevents more than 2 reentrant tool invocations originating from a single model-turn; validated with unit + integration tests
Telemetry surfaced in Console: per-route counts of deferred-synth hits/misses, recursion-sentinel triggers, and shim-fallback events
design_decisions: Deferred synthesis: move from eager marshalling of tool outputs to a lazy serializer that materializes structured JSON only when a downstream consumer (stream sink, compatibility shim, or user request for structured output) reads it
Feedback fence: attach lightweight provenance tokens to injected results; model-driven tool calls check token TTL + origin chain and will be blocked if token depth > 2

Recursion sentinel: central counter in the execution context increments on every model-initiated tool call; when threshold exceeded we surface a RecoverableToolLoopError to the model and fallback to synthesized summary instead of full tool payload
Compatibility shim runs as an opt-in adapter registered per-tool; shim consumes lazy serializer and produces an eager JSON blob for tools with legacy expectations
Streaming integration: streaming sinks (HTTP chunk, websocket) can subscribe to staged patches of the lazy serializer to receive partial structured data without forcing full materialization
implementation_notes: Runtime change: introduce LazyToolPayload type (opaque handle + manifest) in serving-runtime. Payload supports: materialize(), streamPatch(after_cursor), probeStructure()
KV/Cache impact: avoid storing full materialized payload in Redis; store manifest + small anchors. Add GC TTL for manifests to avoid long-lived opaque handles
Scheduler: on materialize(), prefer background worker that can use lower-priority GPU/CPU if request is non-latency-critical (e.g., background analytics), but allow sync path for strict SLO routes
API contract: add optional response header X-Redwood-Deferred: true for responses that used deferred synthesis; add API flag ?force_materialize=true for debugging/clients that need eager outputs
Compatibility shim: implement in python adapter layer for existing internal tools first (search_tool_v1, code_exec_v0). Provide interface to register shim mapping in tool-registry config
Fallback behavior: if materialization fails (OOM, kernel miscompile), fallback to summary + link to original resource and emit shim-fallback telemetry
test_plan: Unit tests for LazyToolPayload materialize()/streamPatch() covering partial reads, concurrent materialize calls, and cancellation
Property tests to ensure provenance tokens can't be forged and depth counting increments exactly at model-initiated boundaries
Integration smoke in runtime-staging: run synthetic mix (60% chat, 30% tool-heavy, 10% streaming) for 24h and compare token costs and latency against baseline
Chaos test: kill materialization worker and verify requests degrade gracefully (summary fallback) and that consumer receives correct error semantics
Compatibility test matrix: run legacy tool contract suite against shim-enabled runtime for search_tool_v1 and code_exec_v0
E2E streaming test: websocket client subscribes to structured stream patches and asserts correct incremental JSON schema fragments
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Feature branch + fsim tests: implement LazyToolPayload with mock tool and land internal API feature flag (runtime-flag: deferred_tool_synthesis=false)
Stage 1 - Canary: enable feature flag for 1% of hosted traffic (non-prod customers) and observe telemetry for 48h
Stage 2 - Staged ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 days with health checks: p99 latency, error rate, recursion-sentinel triggers
Stage 3 - Enterprise opt-outs: add toggle per-customer in dedicated/private for customers who require eager tool outputs by policy
Stage 4 - Deprecation window: after 8 weeks and if metrics stable, consider switching default to deferred=true and mark old eager path for removal in runtime-1.22
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed validating lazy serialization approach with prototype (marcus/eng spike branch). Observed ~14% token cost reduction on contrived doc-lookup workload.
2026-02-20: Design review with PM & DRI (Aisha). Feedback: add explicit API debugging flag and telemetry naming conventions. Action: add X-Redwood-Deferred header and Dashboard tile proposal.
2026-02-27: Initial runtime PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1432 (prototype LazyToolPayload, basic materialize). Needs tests and GC hook. @qa requested integration test plan.

2026-03-03: Compatibility shim prototype (python adapter) implemented for search_tool_v1. Demoed to integrators; noted one edge-case where tool expects streaming newline-delimited JSON — shim now supports newline mode.
2026-03-09: Security review kickoff. Security team asked for threat modeling for provenance tokens (replay/fraud). Decided to sign tokens with per-tenant key and short TTL (30s).

2026-03-12: Integration tests running in runtime-staging. Observed one regression: certain long-lived websocket streams forced full materialization due to existing stream-sink behaviour. Patch queued to expose streamPatch() API in socket layer (PR 1478).
risks: If the lazy serializer leaks references, GC pressure could grow -> mitigate with manifest TTLs and periodic sweep
Model-level adversarial patterns could try to craft tool outputs that force repeated materializations; mitigate via cost-based throttling and circuit-breaker on per-session basis
Compatibility shims increase maintenance burden; we will document shim contract and target shims as short-term bridges only
Telemetry semantics must be clear; misinterpreting deferred hits/misses could lead to incorrect cost allocation for customers
notes: This ticket focuses on the runtime & shim surface area. Separate follow-up (PMTBD) will cover SDK changes (python/go/node) to expose ?force_materialize and debug headers to customers. Coordinate with Console team for Dashboard tile and per-route toggles.
